claims.text: Annual project grants are available to support research into the human past through its material culture or material remains.
The grants cover archaeology, art history, architectural and building history, material culture studies, and the history of collecting.
The grants are for projects where the Society will be the main or a significant financial contributor.
The grants support definable objectives with specific, measurable outcomes within larger projects funded from a range of sources.
Applications are welcomed from early career researchers.
Projects that are innovative in their approach, entail new initiatives, and/or create interdisciplinary interest are welcomed.
Applications must be from the project director or principal investigator.
Work contributing to an undergraduate or postgraduate degree is not funded.
Retrospective applications will not be considered.

Eligible project costs include travel & subsistence for project team members, costs of specialist or scientific investigation, technical services, hire of plant and site accommodation, materials and consumables, and hire of specialist equipment.

Ineligible project costs include personal remuneration, salaries of staff holding current appointments, institutional overheads, internal hire charges, publication subventions and contingency estimates.
Most awards are made on an annual basis with possible renewal for up to two further years.
A new application is required each year, and no project will be funded for more than three years.
Projects should not start before 1 April in the year of application.
Grants should be taken up by 31 December of the year in which they are awarded.
The deadline for applications for Hugh Phillips, Margaret and Tom Jones, Wainwright Research Archaeology in Wales, and Open Research is 15 January each year.
The deadline for references for Hugh Phillips, Margaret and Tom Jones, Wainwright Research Archaeology in Wales, and Open Research is 21 January.
The deadline for applications for Beatrice di Cardi, Janet Arnold, Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler, and William Lambarde is 7 April each year.
The deadline for references for Beatrice di Cardi, Janet Arnold, Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler, and William Lambarde is 14 April.
There are two application rounds for William and Jane Morris Church Conservation grants: 31 March and 31 August every year.
Research and Travel Grants range from £500 to £5,000.
Janet Arnold Awards range from £350 to £5,000.
Beatrice de Cardi Awards range from £5,000 to £15,000.
Margaret and Tom Jones Awards range from £1,000 to £10,500.
Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler Travel Awards are up to £500.
William Lambarde Travel Awards are up to £500.
William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants are between £500 and £5,000.
The Linda Parry Textile Research and Conservation Grants are up to £4000 per project.
Applications must be made via the Grants Application Portal.
Successful applicants must demonstrate they have received all relevant permissions to undertake their project before funds are released.
Unspent award remainder must be returned to the Society for reinvestment.
Successful applicants must submit a report of up to 1,000 words, a financial statement, and two or three digital images by 28 February of the year following the award.
Acknowledgement of the Research Grant in any publication or practical use of the research is required.
The awards are for research into the human past through its material culture or material remains.
